1. **`src/cycles.js:17-22` (`monthlyCents`): monthly costs are still cut off instead of rounded.** The task says every monthly cost should now be rounded to the nearest cent. Both branches still use `Math.floor`, for weekly plans and for the existing monthly/yearly ones.
   - €59.90 a week is 5990 × 52 ÷ 12 = 25956.67 cents, which should show as **€259.57**. Running `subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week` then `subtrack list` shows `€259.56 a month`.
   - The old cycles are wrong too: `subtrack add Backup 119.99 --every year` shows `€9.99 a month`, but 11999 ÷ 12 = 999.92 rounds to **€10.00**.
   - The new tests confirm the wrong values: `test/cycles.test.js` expects `monthlyCents({ price: 5990, cycle: 'weekly' }) === 25956` and the 100-cent case to be 433, and `test/cli.test.js` expects `€259.56 a month`. The existing `€9.99 a month` assertion for Cloud backup in `test/cli.test.js` was left as it is, though it should change.

2. **`bin/subtrack.js` (`total` case): the monthly total is still cut off too.** It still does `Math.floor(... + 1e-9)`, so it isn't rounded like the task asks. With Meal kit €59.90/week, Backup €119.99/year and a €12/week plan, the exact sum is 32156.58 cents. `subtrack total` prints `Monthly total: €321.56 (3 plans)`; rounded, it should be **€321.57**. The new CLI test also asserts the cut-off `Monthly total: €259.56 (1 plan)`. (The single-plan case should be €259.57.)

3. **`src/export.js:7` and `:23`: `subtrack export` writes `NaN` as the monthly cost of weekly plans.** `export.js` keeps its own `MONTHS = { monthly: 1, yearly: 12 }` table and its own `Math.floor(sub.price / MONTHS[sub.cycle])`, and the change didn't touch it. # subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.

# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every month\|week\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. For weekly plans, charges repeat every 7 days. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.
